notes:
Overview: Lyra builds an IDE-integrated copilot (VS Code + JetBrains) focused on ultra-low latency streaming completions for active typing and large context completions. They are very UX-sensitive: users must see incremental tokens with TTFT targets and smooth delivery.

Key ask: low-latency streaming + token budget tuning. Primary objectives: 
 - TTFT (time-to-first-token) target: <= 120ms for single-line completions in 95th pct under office network conditions.
 - Jitter target: per-chunk jitter <30ms; smooth character-level flow.
 - Backpressure handling: graceful slowdown, partial completions, client-side cancellation/resume without corrupting KV cache.
 - Token budgets: dynamic per-session budgets for multi-line suggestions, early-stop heuristics when budgets hit threshold.
 - Model/version pinning: must pin stable model for enterprise release, allow staged rollouts (canary + automatic fallback to smaller quantized model under load).

Technical notes from 2026-03-05 demo (Priya + Derek):
 - Demo showed hosted_api SSE path; good for POC but websocket preferred for live editing (less reconnections, lower TTFT).
 - Observed TTFT ~180-220ms on hosted endpoint across broadband office; jitter spikes during background sync. Customer says: "Feels choppy when files are large / edits are rapid."
 - Token budgeting: want server-side per-session token caps and per-suggestion heuristics (prefer to return short helpful suggestion vs long bloated completion).
 - Prefers explicit token-cost telemetry surfaced to IDE (so product can show estimated consumption for a suggestion).
 - Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations for quantization (INT8) vs throughput trade-offs.

POC scope (agreed): 2-week POC on Dedicated pool with:
 - Websocket streaming endpoint + SDK shim for VS Code extension.
 - Configurable token budget controller (policy: short/medium/long suggestions; preemptive early stop at 85% budget).
 - TTFT instrumentation: client + server side timers; export traces to Redwood Console.
 - Canary rollout mechanism: start pinned model (stable-v1), canary to quantized-v1 for low latency paths, automatic fallback if latency or quality regresses.

Timeline / Activities:
 - 2026-02-18: Lead created (initial inbound trial request).
 - 2026-02-22: Intro call, AE Derek, SE Priya. High-level requirements captured.
 - 2026-02-28: Shared security questionnaire; Lyra requested SOC2 evidence + KMS details. (drive link attached).
 - 2026-03-05: Technical demo + streaming POC scoping (Fireflies FF:2026-03-05-lyra-lowlatency-demo).
 - 2026-03-09: Security team sent VPC network diagram and asked for egress policy details.

Quotes / customer language (paraphrased):
 - "We need typing to feel continuous. If the copilot stutters, adoption drops."
 - "Token budget controls are critical — devs will rage at over-long suggestions that eat credits."

Integration notes / risks:
 - VS Code extension team needs an SDK shim to handle chunk reassembly and out-of-order partials. We should mock the client-side buffer in POC.
 - Long-lived websocket tunnels across corporate proxies: risk of intermittent resets. Need reconnect/backoff strategy and server-side session resumption (KV cache).
 - Data residency: Lyra wants EU-only storage for EU customers; will require Private or Dedicated with region pinning.

Commercial: Lyra prefers Dedicated if latency gains are material. Budget sensitivity: mid-market ARR band. Proposed commercial motion: 6-12 month reserved Dedicated pool + Optimize add-on.

Next steps (short):
 - Ship POC artifact: websocket SDK shim + sample VS Code integration by 2026-03-12.
 - SE to provide Dedicated perf estimate + pricing (Priya).
 - Security to respond to VPC egress Qs (Marta to coordinate).
